cells.tense: You're the one tending what's worth keeping, and you know it.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: a place of steady forward motion toward what you've decided matters
cells.ask: Offer one thing you made visible to the people who'd honor it. What comes back is release — completions you no longer have to carry.
cells.core: You're the one tending what's worth carrying forward, and you're doing it deliberately — deciding what grows and giving it the form it needs. Not force and not drift. Your momentum has soil under it: things are growing because you're tending them, and you know the difference between care and control. That balance between competing demands isn't strain; it's grace, and it's what keeps the whole thing moving.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what matters with both hands, and you know it.

cells.tense: You're already out ahead of what's actually here.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: a place of steady forward motion toward what you've decided matters
cells.ask: Slow to the pace of what you're actually tending. Let one thing be finished before you imagine the next. What comes back is vision that rises from what you've lived — satisfaction that doesn't have to be manufactured.
cells.core: You're driving toward a future so hard you've stopped being in the one you're in. Every part of what you tend gets pushed to become what it could be — the project, the people, the pace itself — and the pushing is doing the opposite of what pushing was for. You're clutching at growth to make it happen faster, and care that clutches exhausts both the cared-for and the one caring. The vision you're chasing has gotten ahead of the life that would feed it.
cells.sheetLine: You're forcing growth that would come on its own.

cells.tense: You stopped at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: a place of steady forward motion toward what you've decided matters
cells.ask: Follow one thing you've already started through to its finish. Let yourself keep hoping about it past the point where it stopped being easy. What comes back is shining from real development — not wanting to shine, but growing until the light is what's left.
cells.core: Something you used to tend, you've stopped tending. The care didn't disappear — you put it down somewhere back there and haven't gone back for it — so the direction toward what mattered has gone quiet. You're not moving toward anything you've claimed. It isn't that the capacity is gone. It's that you haven't been reaching for it.
cells.sheetLine: You put it down, and you haven't picked it back up.

cells.tense: You're already keeping this, and you're calling it just your days.
cells.verb: tending what grows with responsible care
cells.place: a place of steady forward motion toward what you've decided matters
cells.ask: Admit that one thing you keep steady is being kept steady by you. Say it to someone and let them see what it costs. What comes back is release — finishing what you started, not carrying it forever.
cells.core: You are keeping something steady right now — holding two demands together, showing up for what you promised, giving your care a form that lasts — and you'd tell me it's just what anyone would do. The tending is doing real work every day, and no one is calling it yours, including the one person whose credit it is. You're already the steward. You just haven't said so.
cells.sheetLine: You're doing the keeping. You call it just your days.
